precepts.text: Samuel's sons took bribes, so the elders asked for a king like all the nations, and it displeased Samuel. The Lord said, They have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them. The law was written knowing Israel would reject him; so he came down through David's loins to be king over them anyway.
precepts.point: When thou shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations, thou shalt set him king whom the Lord shall choose, one from among thy brethren, not a stranger. The law allowed a king, chosen by God from our own people, which rules out voting.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 17:14-15 is law. If, when you get into your land, you decide you want a king like all the nations round about, the law says fine: set a king over you. But “whom the Lord thy God shall choose”: God has to choose him, you cannot. He must be “one from among thy brethren”, of your own people, and “thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother”: do not set a heathen over you. That scratches our voting right there.

Now 1 Samuel 8. “when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel”, Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba. “And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” So the elders of Israel gathered to Samuel at Ramah and said, “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

That is exactly what the law allowed. Samuel was righteous, and he was a priest, so it should not have been a problem. Yet “the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.” Why would something found in the law upset such a righteous man? The Lord answers: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

That is why the law is there. The Lord knew Israel would want to be like the other nations, the Hamites, the Arabs, and would reject him ruling over them from the throne above. So he said: I have something for them. I will come down through David's loins and be king over them anyway, either up here or down there. We should not want a king over us; we have a king right there.

The Lord saw it before it happened. Israel was appointed, predestined, to desire a king over them and to reject him, and he came and ruled over them on the throne down here regardless. That goes to another level, a class in itself.

precepts.text: Thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
precepts.point: Your vote does not choose the ruler. God sets the base men over Israel so they see what it means to want another nation to rule them.

note.label: Latinos For Trump: Alien Vs. Predator

precepts.why:
“the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” It does not matter who you vote for; he puts whoever he wants. Donald Trump is one of the basest of men, a caricature and TV personality from The Apprentice, just as Ronald Reagan was an actor. His orange skin is telling you what he is about: he is Esau, the red man. The Most High puts these men over us so we can see: you wanted the other nations to rule over you besides me, and this is what happens.

Deuteronomy 17:14 shows that desire in our people: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”. We are not satisfied with the King of kings and Lord of lords, Christ, being over us. We always want to be like the other nations. That is why we dye our hair blonde, put in the contacts, put on the suit and tie, go to their universities and get their education, and assimilate to their way of life.

But the law says “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.” We have to have a king of our own people, who is for our people, not a base man out for the interest of corporations that rob and steal our resources. We are not supposed to vote for other nations to be over us. Thus saith the Lord.

The same goes for our people in Latin America. In Mexico and in Argentina, where an Italian was set up, what are they doing for you? Nothing, not a damn thing. You cannot set up people of other nations over you. That is why the Most High sets the basest of men over Israel: to show us what it means to choose a stranger over the king he chose.

precepts.point: The leaders people admire are the base men God has set up for this time.

precepts.text: Enquire diligently, and behold, if it be true and the thing certain; the diligent enquiry that governs how the witness law is applied.
precepts.point: A lot of people do not know how to apply this verse; the precept for Leviticus 5:1 is Deuteronomy 17:4. Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed: make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

note.label: Leviticus 5: The Trespass Offering and the Duty of the Witness

precepts.why:
A lot of people do not know how to apply Leviticus 5:1, and this is its precept. “And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel”.

Whether the thing be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only when it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed. The witness who has seen or known of it must utter it, but make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment.

precepts.text: At the mouth of two or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; one witness is never enough.
precepts.point: The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“Whoso killeth any person, the murderer shall be put to death by the mouth of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any person to cause him to die.” Witnesses, plural: “At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.”

Multiple people must testify, and their stories must match in the details for the murder to be established. One witness alone is never enough to put a man to death, because a single witness could lie in the interest of the avenger and put an innocent man to death.

precepts.text: If a soul hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; the witness law is applied through the diligent enquiry of Deuteronomy 17:4.
precepts.point: Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

note.label: Deuteronomy 17: Idolatry Judged and the Duty of a King

precepts.why:
“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A lot of people do not know how to apply Leviticus 5:1; the precept for it is Deuteronomy 17:4.

The witness who has seen or known of a thing must utter it, and here is what is done with what he utters: “And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel”. Whether it be told thee or thou hast heard of it, thou shalt enquire diligently, and only if it be true and the thing certain does judgment proceed.

So the witness law of Leviticus is applied through the diligent enquiry of Deuteronomy 17:4. Make sure you are certain of a thing before you bring somebody to judgment; only after diligent enquiry was the man or woman that served other gods, the sun or moon or any of the host of heaven, brought to the gates and stoned with stones till they die.

precepts.text: Every king of Israel had to write himself a copy of the law and read therein all the days of his life, not just on a sabbath, that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep the words of this law to do them; you are what you eat, and what you put within comes out in your conversation and your actions.
precepts.point: That thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: the end goal of talking about the commandments and meditating on the commandments is to do the commandments. Attending every class, hearing every breakdown, and keeping every precept list is all in vain if you never do thus saith the Lord; not doing the word of God is why we went into slavery and sit at the bottom of society.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
Every king of Israel had the same charge Joshua got: “when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them”.

He had to write himself a copy of the law and read therein all the days of his life, not just on a sabbath, that he may learn to fear the Lord and keep the words of this law to do them. You are what you eat, and what you put within comes out in your conversation and your actions. That is the law in the mouth, the meditation day and night, and the observing to do, all in one charge to the king.

precepts.text: At the mouth of two witnesses or three witnesses shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
precepts.point: These cities were appointed for all the children of Israel and for the stranger that sojourneth among them, that whosoever killeth any person at unawares might flee thither and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation: until he gets a fair trial.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The cities were appointed so that the one who killed at unawares would “not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stood before the congregation”: until he gets a fair trial. That trial had a standard. “At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.”

No man was put to death on one man's word. This law of righteous judgment is what is missing in the cursed cities of our people, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, who have not learned to apply the scripture and await righteous trial.

precepts.text: Moses prophesied that Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me; Moses was shown from the beginning to the end, he saw Israel rejecting the Lord, and he wrote it for us to read.
precepts.point: Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
Moses prophesied this very moment: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me.”

And that is what the elders said at Ramah: “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.” Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. Moses was shown from the beginning to the end; he saw Israel rejecting the Lord, and he wrote it for us to read.

Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

precepts.text: The king was to be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
precepts.point: Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
The law set the king: “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.”

Israel asked for a king “like all the nations”, not one whom the Lord would choose. When we rejected the Lord in our own land, that also set us up to be taken out of our own land and set in a land we did not know, under oppressors: strangers over us.

Now you hear people say, well, this one is the lesser of two evils; but they are both evil. We look at our condition now because this is what we sought: we rejected the Lord and said we want a king over us, we want to be like all the other nations.

precepts.text: Moses prophesied Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Moses saw this coming long before it happened. In the spirit of the Lord he knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and he wrote it down ahead of time: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”.

That is what Samuel is rebuking. When Nahash the king of the children of Ammon came against them, Israel said, “Nay; but a king shall reign over us: when the Lord your God was your king.” They wanted a king they could see and touch, because all the nations around them had kings. That demand exposed their disbelief in the Lord, and Moses had already written it down.

precepts.text: The king must be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
The same law that foresaw the demand set its terms: “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.”

So when Samuel says, “behold, the Lord hath set a king over you”, the king stands under the law Moses wrote ahead of time: one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren, never a stranger.

precepts.text: His heart must not be lifted up above his brethren, and he must not turn aside from the commandment to the right hand or to the left, to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he and his children in the midst of Israel; that is exactly what Samuel just told the people.
precepts.point: Moses, in the spirit of the Lord, knew exactly what Israel would do once they came into the land, and wrote the law of the king ahead of time.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
The law of the king ends on the very terms Samuel just laid before the people. The king must walk so “That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Israel.”

Samuel says the same: “If ye will fear the Lord, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall both ye and also the king that reigneth over you continue following the Lord your God”. If you and your king do not rebel against the voice of the Lord, the ultimate king, you will be all right. The king who turns not aside prolongs his days in his kingdom, he and his children.

precepts.text: The king shall not multiply wives to himself, nor greatly multiply silver and gold, which is exactly what Solomon did.
precepts.point: He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away: neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.”

That is exactly what Solomon did. “And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.” The law told the king why not to multiply wives, “that his heart turn not away”, and it turned away just as it said.

precepts.text: The king was to write himself a copy of the law and read in it all his life, that he learn to fear the Most High and not lift himself above his brethren.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
The law set the king’s duty plainly: “when he sitteth upon the throne of his kingdom, that he shall write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests the Levites: And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life: that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law and these statutes, to do them”.

The king was to write himself a copy of the law and read in it all his life, that he learn to fear the Most High and not lift himself above his brethren. Uzziah did the opposite: “his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against the Lord his God”. Had he kept the law before him, he would have known the incense was not his to burn.
